articles.title: OpenAI reportedly raises an additional $11 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation
articles.snippet: OpenAI has reportedly raised an additional $11 billion as part of a funding round that hasn't closed yet but is expected to in the coming weeks.
articles.text:
In Brief
Posted:
2:53 PM PST · November 6, 2026
Image Credits: Samuel Boivin/NurPhoto / Getty Images
Lucas Ropek
OpenAI reportedly raises an additional $11 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation
OpenAI has reportedly raised $11 billion so far in a new funding round that values the AI lab at $1.25 trillion.
Bloomberg reported on the new funding on Friday, citing sources familiar with the matter. The $11 billion is part of a larger funding round that hasn’t closed yet, according to the outlet. The round is expected to close in the coming weeks and could total about $20 billion, a source told Bloomberg.
In late September, Bloomberg reported that OpenAI was looking to raise $30 billion in the upcoming round. The current figures fall well short of that target.
TechCrunch has reached out to OpenAI for comment and will update this story if it responds.
The news comes only hours after Bloomberg also reported that potential buyers of shares in the IPO of OpenAI’s chief competitor, Anthropic, are eyeing a substantially lower valuation than Anthropic had targeted. Bloomberg writes that some potential buyers believe Anthropic’s valuation could be as low as $1.1 trillion, compared with the $2 trillion that investors were said to be expecting roughly a month ago.
OpenAI previously intimated that it would go public this year but subsequently delayed its plans. There are expectations that the company will IPO next year at some point.
The market for AI hangs in a particularly precarious place. The Democratic landslide in the U.S. midterms — and overwhelmingly negative voter sentiment around data centers — has caused jitters throughout the market , with many anticipating potential regulatory challenges in the future.

Shield Announces $5.3 Billion Echodyne Acquisition and $2.5 Billion Funding Raise
Shield AI has announced a definitive agreement to acquire radar technology manufacturer Echodyne Corporation in a transaction valued at up to $5.3 billion, alongside a $2.5 billion financing package intended to support the acquisition and expand the company’s autonomous defense and counter-unmanned aircraft systems capabilities.
The Shield Echodyne acquisition will bring Echodyne’s compact, software-defined radar technology into Shield AI’s Mission Systems business, strengthening its portfolio of autonomous aircraft, artificial intelligence software and advanced sensing systems.
The financing includes $1 billion in Series H funding at a $28.8 billion post-money valuation, a $1 billion structured equity investment from funds managed by Blackstone and $500 million in debt financing led by JPMorgan Chase Bank.
The transaction is expected to close in early 2027, subject to regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions.
Shield Echodyne Acquisition Valued at $5.3 Billion
Under the definitive agreement, Shield AI will acquire Echodyne in a transaction valued at up to $5.3 billion.
The purchase consideration includes $4.8 billion payable or issuable at closing, with an additional $500 million contingent on Echodyne meeting agreed performance targets.
Echodyne develops compact radar systems used in counter-drone operations, airspace security and defense applications.
Its products are integrated into hundreds of counter-UAS and security systems serving defense, government and commercial customers in more than 40 countries.
The acquisition is intended to expand Shield AI’s capabilities in sensing, threat detection and autonomous defense systems.
Both companies expect triple-digit revenue growth during the current fiscal year, according to the announcement.
Shield AI Raises $2.5 Billion to Support Acquisition
Shield AI is assembling a $2.5 billion financing package to support the transaction.
The financing consists of three components:
Financing Source Amount
Series H equity funding $1 billion
Blackstone-managed structured equity investment $1 billion
Debt financing led by JPMorgan Chase $500 million
Total financing $2.5 billion
The Series H round values Shield AI at $28.8 billion on a post-money basis.
The round is co-led by Disruptive and Innovation X Capital, with participation from Advent, JPMorganChase’s Strategic Investment Group, Snowpoint Ventures, Apandion, Center15 Capital and other investors.
Shield AI said the Series H proceeds will be used primarily to finance the acquisition.
Echodyne Radar Technology Expands Counter-UAS Capabilities
Echodyne designs and manufactures compact, solid-state radar systems using its patented Metamaterials Electronically Scanned Array (MESA) technology.
The radar systems are designed to detect and track aerial objects, including small unmanned aircraft that can be difficult to identify using conventional sensing technologies.
Echodyne’s products support several counter-UAS applications:
Drone detection and tracking
Military base protection
Border security
Critical infrastructure protection

articles.title: Shield AI Funding: $2.5B Raise, $28.8B Valuation and Echodyne Deal
articles.snippet: Shield AI Funding: $2.5B Raise, $28.8B Valuation and Echodyne Deal AI Funding Tracker
articles.text:
Shield AI agreed on November 5, 2026, to buy radar maker Echodyne in a deal valued at $5.3 billion. To pay for it, the San Diego defense company is raising $2.5 billion in new capital.
The package includes a $1 billion Series H at a $28.8 billion post-money valuation. That is more than double the $12.7 billion valuation Shield AI recorded in March 2026.
Crunchbase News ranked the $2 billion equity portion as the largest U.S. startup round for the week of October 31 to November 6.
Shield AI funding: how the $2.5 billion package breaks down
The financing has three parts, according to Shield AI’s announcement. Two are equity and one is debt.
Component Amount Provider Terms disclosed
Series H equity $1.0 billion Co-led by Disruptive and Innovation X Capital $28.8 billion post-money valuation
Structured equity $1.0 billion Funds managed by Blackstone Not disclosed
Debt financing $0.5 billion JPMorgan Chase Bank, sole arranger Not disclosed
Total $2.5 billion Three sources Proceeds go mainly to the Echodyne deal
Shield AI said Series H proceeds will go mainly toward the Echodyne purchase. The $2.5 billion raised equals about 47% of the $5.3 billion deal value.
Blackstone has backed Shield AI before. In March 2026, its funds provided $500 million in fixed-return preferred equity next to the Series G.
Shield AI valuation history from 2022 to 2026
Shield AI’s valuation rose from $2.3 billion in mid-2022 to $28.8 billion in November 2026. Most of that gain came in the past 20 months.
Date Round Amount raised Post-money valuation
June 2022 Series E $165 million $2.3 billion
October 2023 Series F $200 million $2.7 billion
March 2025 Series F-1 $240 million $5.3 billion
March 2026 Series G $1.5 billion plus $500 million preferred $12.7 billion
November 2026 Series H $1.0 billion plus $1.5 billion other capital $28.8 billion
The move from $12.7 billion to $28.8 billion is a 127% increase in about eight months. Against the March 2025 mark of $5.3 billion, the valuation has grown about 5.4 times.
Shield AI’s March round placed it among the top-funded AI startups of Q1 2026 . Advent International and the Strategic Investment Group of JPMorganChase’s Security and Resiliency Initiative co-led that round. Part of the money went toward buying flight simulation company Aechelon.
Why Shield AI is buying Echodyne
CEO Gary Steele described the company as three business units: autonomy software, autonomous systems and mission systems. Echodyne joins the mission systems unit.
Shield AI already sells Hivemind autonomy software, the V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation tools. Echodyne adds radars that detect and track drones, which counter-drone systems need before they can act.
Echodyne’s radar business and contracts
Echodyne is based in Kirkland, Washington. It builds solid-state radars with its patented Metamaterials Electronically Scanned Array (MESA) design.
Its radars sit inside hundreds of counter-drone and security systems. Defense, government and commercial customers in more than 40 countries use them.
In September, Echodyne won a contract with a $250 million ceiling from Joint Interagency Task Force 401. The contract covers counter-drone radar for U.S. and allied forces.
The same radars have civilian uses. Stadiums and airports use them to spot unauthorized drones, and police and fire departments use them to fly their own drones in shared airspace.

This is a weekly feature that runs down the week’s Top 10 announced funding rounds in the U.S. Check out last week’s biggest funding deal roundup here .
This week brought another plethora of large funding rounds for startups and growth-stage companies. Shield AI , a defense tech player focused on autonomy and virtual simulations, secured the largest financing, bringing in $2 billion. Next on the list was drone delivery provider Zipline International , which pulled in a fresh $1.5 billion.
Rounding out the ranks were good-sized financings for sectors including agentic AI, space tech and AI infrastructure.
1. Shield AI , $2B, defense tech: Shield AI, a developer of autonomy software and systems for the defense sector, along with simulation and synthetic reality technologies, secured $2 billion in equity funding and $500 million in debt financing. The equity included a $1 billion Series H led by Disruptive and Innovation X Capital along with a $1 billion structured equity investment from funds managed by Blackstone . The $500 million debt financing was led by JPMorganChase . San Diego-based Shield also said it is acquiring radar company Echodyne in a transaction valued at $5.3 billion.
2. Zipline International , $1.5B, drones: Drone delivery provider Zipline International raised $1.5 billion in late-stage funding at a $21.5 billion post-money valuation. Paradigm , WCM Investment Management and Layer Global led the financing for the South San Francisco, California-based company, which plans to use the money to expand its U.S. manufacturing facilities and increase hiring as it builds a nationwide drone delivery network.
3. CesiumAstro , $730M, space tech: Austin-based CesiumAstro, a developer of space and defense communications systems and satellites, closed on $730 million in Series D financing at a valuation of more than $4.5 billion. Janus Henderson led the equity round, and the company also secured $100 million in debt financing through the Export-Import Bank of the United States and JP Morgan .
4. Northwood Space , $375M, space tech: Torrance, California-based Northwood Space, a developer of ground infrastructure to support satellite systems, picked up $375 million in Series C funding. Andreessen Horowitz and DFJ Growth led the financing for the 3-year-old startup, which raised its Series B about nine months ago.
5. Applied Compute , $350M, AI models: Applied Compute, provider of a cloud computing platform that enterprises and developers use to train and run large AI models, announced $350 million in new funding at a $3.25 billion valuation. Elad Gil led the financing, joined by a long list of investors including Nvidia . The San Francisco-based company, which launched 18 months ago, said its annual recurring revenue has already topped $100 million.
